headline: High-risk shared-workspace orchestration: Langflow can write and egress by default, while RisingWave’s interaction surface is undocumented, creating leakage and conflict uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write the server filesystem and chain tools in graph flows, so attacker-controlled content can become instructions if it is fed into a flow. RisingWave has no documented input surface here, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are copied into a Langflow flow node or uploaded file
IF Langflow parses file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to every imported artifact
Disable automatic instruction-following on file inputs
Require a human review step before routing external text into flows
Use separate workspaces for generated content and untrusted inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, uploaded files, and stored credentials, and it has broad network egress. RisingWave is documented as network-egress none, but its lack of file/workspace details means the shared-data path is incomplete; still, Langflow alone can expose sensitive flow data if paired through a shared workspace.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem or workspace
IF Langflow flow inputs include secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Keep Langflow and RisingWave on separate volumes
Store secrets outside shared flow inputs
Restrict Langflow outbound destinations to allowlisted endpoints
Rotate any credentials that were placed in flow stores

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the filesystem, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no concurrency details provided. Because shared mutable-resource overlap is plausible but not documented, the conflict risk is real yet uncertain, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF an orchestrator does not provide locking or isolation
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable package installation in shared environments
Run each agent under distinct OS users
Add file locks around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based flow system that can chain multiple agents, so its outputs can become downstream inputs. RisingWave is a data-engineering backend, but no verification or approval boundary is documented here; the pair therefore supports an A-to-B propagation path, though not enough to justify high severity.
conditions: IF Langflow output is used as an input to a RisingWave job or pipeline
IF no validation step checks schema, provenance, or correctness
mitigations: Insert schema validation between agents
Require explicit approval before downstream execution
Log and diff intermediate outputs before ingestion
Reject free-form text where structured data is expected

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and handles flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while RisingWave’s compliance posture is undocumented in the profile. No specific residency or certification mismatch is evidenced, so only a low compliance gap is supportable; the other agent is not cited beyond its lack of documented controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Langflow flow stores
IF RisingWave is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than Langflow
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in flow credentials
Document retention for flow inputs and outputs
Separate regulated workloads from general workflows
Review deployment residency before processing sensitive data
